chords to the Morning Star?

Hey Everyone,

I have been listening alot to The Orange Tree, by Grey Larsen and Paddy League. I am trying to pick up some of Paddy’s DADGAD playing, which is hard at best.

Right i have been trying to figure out The Morning Star. I play it on flute, so i figured since i know the melody backing it up would be cake. Not so, i have a few chords figured out, but am far from done.

Can anyone just the basic chord structure perhaps? Paddy does some nifty bass line counter point stuff, but i would happy with the basic chords right now.

Morningstar River

Always thought this was a nice name on a tune. Then I was doing a bit of work recently down around Tipperary & Limerick and there is a river there called the Morningstar. Drains the north side of the Ballyhoura Hills and flows out past Kilmallock, thence to the Shannon estuary. It’s as likely a connection as any..?

The Morning Stars

Nice one, wounded hussar.
I’ve wondered where the name comes from for years.
The Hibernian Telegraph, published for a short period between 1799 and 1799(!), in Dublin, was also known, it seems, as the Morning Star and was one of the first paper to be called so. (Many others would follow, both in the UK and the US)
There’s a 100 y.o. pub in Belfast city center called the Morning Star.

The Morning Star, X:10

This setting from the great Denis “the Weaver” Murphy of Lisheen. Denis recorded it as a solo track on the famous “Star Above the Garter” album, in which he plays Kerry music with his sister, Julia Clifford. Denis’s playing and variations are nothing but lovely, particularly in the way that he ends the B part before the turn. Denis followed it with another single reel, Rolling in the Ryegrass ( https://thesession.org/tunes/87 ).

Re: The Morning Star

Calling all pipers, any one figured out what tight triplets Paddy Keenan plays around the B in bars 1 and 5 on the record and on the Bothy Band YouTube set, tried a few but nothing sounds right….could be me I suppose…?

↳ Posted by Eagach on March 12th, 2018.

Re: The Morning Star

They’re just staccato BcB triplets. Close the chanter between each note. Use only the top hand index finger for the staccato c, keep everything else closed up.

Were you getting hung up on the fact that the tune is in G and a desire to be tonally correct by using a cross fingered C natural instead?

Don’t do that. Staccato c has no key signature, no tonality at all, really. It is purely percussive.

Watch Paddy’s hands here very closely:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I3oO6I56Guc

Notice he doesn’t open any bottom hand toneholes while playing the BCB triplet, and his top hand index finger barely moves at all.

↳ Posted by MP1996 on March 12th, 2018.

Re: The Morning Star

If you were asking about the BCD triplets, the same rule applies: use staccato C, close the chanter between each note.

↳ Posted by MP1996 on March 12th, 2018.
